evidence: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:534 and :537 call r.log.Error("Annotations to clean by time", ...) / r.log.Error("cleaned annotations by time", ...) on every batch of the normal, successful cleanup path. Nothing has failed at that point; line 534 even dumps the full 'ids' slice (up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize entries) and the SQL condition. These look like leftover debug statements. Together with the cleanup ticker being cut from 10m to 1m (pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go:77), they will fill error logs and can trigger error-rate alerts. They should be Debug, or removed.

xorm_store.go:530-533: 'ids, err := r.fetchIDs(...); if err != nil { return 0, err }'. So when line 534 logs "err", err, err is always nil. The same dead field appears at :554 (after the early return at :551-553) and :576 (after :573-575). The field adds nothing and can be dropped as part of the log cleanup in issue 0.

xorm_store.go:554 and :557 have the same problem as issue 0 in the MaxCount path: r.log.Error("Annotations to clean by count", ... "ids", ids ...) and r.log.Error("cleaned annotations by count", ...) run on every successful batch. They should be Debug, or removed.

xorm_store.go:576 and :579 in CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags have the same problem: r.log.Error("Tags to clean", ... "ids", ids ...) and r.log.Error("cleaned tags", ...) log routine per-batch progress at Error level. They should be Debug, or removed.

xorm_store.go:608 checks 'r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > sqliteParameterLimit' rather than 'len(ids) > sqliteParameterLimit'. The observation is accurate: on SQLite with a batch size over 999, even a short final batch goes down the inlined-literal branch (:609-613). There is no correctness or security impact, though. fetchIDs returns ids as []int64 (:590), formatted with %d, so the literal SQL is safe and returns the same result. The only cost is that the statement is not parameterised for small batches, which is negligible. The claim that this is 'unnecessary' is right, but its impact is overstated. Switching to len(ids) would be slightly more precise and is easy to do, but it isn't required.
